\begin{lemma}[Product of threshold signs]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_thresholdSign_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_thresholdSign_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianCDF_zero, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{6}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X,Y:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ each have
the standard Gaussian distribution under $\mu$. Define $\sigma(r)=1$ for $r\ge0$ and
$\sigma(r)=-1$ for $r<0$. Then $\int \sigma(X)\sigma(Y)\,d\mu=4\mu(X\le0,\,Y\le0)-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Stability of a homogeneous Gaussian halfspace]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability_homogeneous_halfspace}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability_homogeneous_halfspace}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_fst, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_projection, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_snd, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_thresholdSign_mul, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianProjection, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianQuadrantProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sheppard_formula, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$.
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the Gaussian noise stability of the sign function
$x\mapsto\sigma\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\right)$ is $1-2\arccos(\rho)/\pi$.
\end{theorem}
